executive_brief: The Enhanced Expense Tracker is a CLI-based financial application utilizing a strict 3-tier architecture (CLI -> Service -> Repository) with SQLite persistence. It provides core CRUD capabilities for expense tracking, emphasizing rigorous input validation, atomic transactions, and a Test-Driven Development (TDD) approach to ensure data integrity and structural isolation.

architectural_constraints: Strict 3-layer separation: CLI (I/O), Service (Business Logic/Validation), Repository (Data Access)
Transaction integrity: Mandatory atomic commit/rollback for all write operations (Create, Delete)
Performance threshold: Listing/filtering < 1,000 records must execute in < 1 second
QA Gate: 100% of invalid inputs must be intercepted by Service Layer before reaching Repository
QA Gate: 100% of data modifications must be atomic
Zero leakage: No SQL in CLI/Service; no CLI logic in Repository/Service

maturity_assessment: The specifications exhibit a high level of technical rigor and structural completeness. The definition of explicit error mappings and measurable success criteria ensures an objective implementation path. While there is a minor gap regarding the formal documentation of unresolved uncertainties concerning SQLite concurrency, the provided edge cases address most common failures. Status: READY.
critical_dependencies: Pytest framework for mandatory TDD execution
Integrity: Expense entity strictly dependent on unique integer ID for deletion operations
Relational: Mandatory mapping of Service-level exceptions (EntityNotFoundError, ValidationError) to CLI user messages
Relational: Mapping of Repository-level DatabaseLockedError to CLI user messages
